people.name: Oritsé Williams
people.description: British singer Oritsé Williams is best known as the founding member of the boy band JLS, who finished as runners-up to Alexandra Burke on the fifth series of The X Factor in 2008. The group's first two singles, 'Beat Again' and 'Everybody in Love', both reached No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart. Before disbanding in December 2013, JLS sold over 10 million records.

people.name: Professor Green
people.description: Stephen Manderson is an English pop artist, rapper, singer, and songwriter who performs under the stage name Professor Green or simply Pro Green. His 2010 second single, 'Just Be Good to Green', featured British singer Lily Allen and reached the top 5 in the UK.

people.name: Mike Skinner
people.description: English rapper, singer-songwriter, musician, and record producer Mike Skinner is known as The Streets and secured a 2004 UK No.1 album with A Grand Don't Come For Free. Skinner has additionally put out music under his own name, in the group D.O.T. alongside frequent collaborator Rob Harvey, and utilizing the pseudonym The Darker the Shadow the Brighter the Light.

people.name: Twista
people.description: Twista, also known as Tung Twista and born Carl Terrell Mitchell, is a US rapper who was once recognized as the fastest rap delivery artist in the world. He achieved a US No. 1 album in 2004 with Kamikaze and a US No. 1 single with Slow Jamz.

people.name: Myles Kennedy
people.description: American singer, guitarist, and songwriter Myles Kennedy serves as the lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist for the rock band Alter Bridge, as well as for Slash featuring Myles Kennedy and the Conspirators.

people.name: Fiachna O'Braonain
people.description: Fiachna O'Braonain is a member of the Irish rock band Hothouse Flowers, which achieved a No.11 single in the UK in 1988 with 'Don't Go'. The group's debut album, People, came out in 1988 and stands as the most successful debut record in Irish history, claiming the top spot in Ireland in just one week and later peaking at No.2 on the UK Albums Chart.

people.name: Wallis Buchannan
people.description: Wallis Buchannan performed with Jamiroquai, a group that achieved a UK No.1 album in 1993 with Emergency on Planet Earth and a UK No.1 single in 1998 with 'Deeper Underground'. The band has received a Grammy Award in 1998 and attained worldwide sales of more than 26 million albums.

people.name: Charlie Benante
people.description: American musician Charlie Benante is primarily known for playing drums in the thrash metal band Anthrax and the crossover thrash band Stormtroopers of Death. Anthrax is regarded as one of the pioneering groups of the 1980s thrash metal movement.

people.name: Mike Bordin
people.description: Mike Bordin is the drummer of the American rock band Faith No More. Their version of The Commodores song 'I'm Easy' became a hit single in 1993, reaching No. 3 in the UK and No. 4 in the US. The band also released the best-selling albums The Real Thing in 1989 and Angel Dust in 1992.

people.name: Calvin Hayes
people.description: Calvin Hayes was a member of the British band Johnny Hates Jazz, which achieved international success and a No.5 single on the UK chart in 1987 with 'Shattered Dreams'. The single also reached No.2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent one week at the top of Billboard's Adult Contemporary chart. Hayes passed away at the age of 63 on 10th July 2026, following a collapse at his home in Washington.

people.name: Ashley Ingram
people.description: Ashley Ingram is a singer in the English trio Imagination, which scored a UK No. 2 single in 1982 with 'Just An Illusion'. The group achieved hits across 28 countries and collected four platinum discs, nine gold discs, and upwards of a dozen silver discs globally from 1981 to 1983.

people.name: Charlie Burchill
people.description: Charlie Burchill is the guitarist for the Scottish rock band Simple Minds. The group achieved a 1985 US No.1 single with 'Don't You, Forget About Me' and a 1989 UK No.1 single with 'Belfast Child', along with more than 20 additional UK Top 40 singles. In 2016, they received the British Academy's Ivor Novello Award for Outstanding Song Collection.

people.name: Randy Brecker
people.description: Randy Brecker was a member of the American jazz-rock band Blood Sweat & Tears. The group achieved a US No. 2 single in 1969 with "Spinning Wheel" and a US No. 12 single in 1969 with "You've Made Me So Very Happy". Their second album, Blood, Sweat & Tears, reached No. 1 in the US in 1968.

people.name: Trevor Davis
people.description: Trevor Davis played in the British pop/rock band Dave Dee, Dozy, Beaky, Mick and Tich, which achieved a UK No.1 single in 1968 with 'Legend Of Xanadu'. Following a short illness, Davis passed away in hospital on 13th January 2015.

people.name: Jimi Hendrix
people.description: American guitarist, singer, and songwriter Jimi Hendrix. Hendrix moved to England in late 1966, after bassist Chas Chandler of the Animals became his manager. He had the 1967 UK No.6 single 'Hey Joe', the 1970 UK No.1 single 'Voodoo Chile', and his third and final studio album Electric Ladyland (1968) peaked at No.1 in the US. Hendrix who is widely considered to be the greatest guitarist in musical history, made appearances at the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival, the iconic 1969 Woodstock Festival and the 1970 Isle Of Wight Festival. He was one of the first guitarists to make extensive use of tone-altering effects units in mainstream rock, such as fuzz distortion, Octavia, wah-wah, and Uni-Vibe and was the first musician to use stereophonic phasing effects in recordings. Hendrix died on 18th September 1970 after choking on his own vomit.

people.name: Eddie Rabbitt
people.description: Eddie Rabbitt was a singer and songwriter known for his 1981 US No. 1 hit "I Love A Rainy Night". His compositions were recorded by Elvis Presley, Dr Hook, and Tom Jones. Rabbitt passed away from cancer on May 7th, 1998.

people.name: Buzz Cason
people.description: Buzz Cason was an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. He helped establish The Casuals, which was Nashville's initial rock and roll band. Working alongside Leon Russell as a session musician, Cason produced The Crickets's rendition of 'La Bamba'. Additionally, he provided backing vocals for Elvis Presley as well as Kenny Rogers. Cason passed away in Franklin, Tennessee, on 16 June 2024 at 84 years old.

people.name: Henri Belolo
people.description: French music producer and songwriter Henri Belolo co-created musical acts such as The Ritchie Family and Village People alongside Jacques Morali. He passed away on 3 August 2019 in Paris, France at the age of 82.

people.name: Al Jackson
people.description: Al Jackson was an American songwriter, producer, and drummer. As a founding member of Booker T. and the MG's, the house band for Stax Records, he contributed to the 1962 US No. 3 single 'Green Onions' and the 1969 UK No. 4 single 'Time Is Tight'. Known for his drumming skill, he was affectionately called "The Human Timekeeper". Throughout his career, Jackson collaborated with numerous performers, such as Rufus Thomas, Al Green, Carla Thomas, Eddie Floyd, Sam & Dave, Otis Redding, Elvis Presley, Bill Withers, Wilson Pickett, Leon Russell, Jerry Lee Lewis, Eric Clapton, Aretha Franklin, and blues guitarist Albert King. On October 1st, 1975, Jackson was shot and killed by burglars inside his home.

works.title: All Too Well
works.eventDescription: Taylor Swift achieved a No. 1 on the US Hot 100 with the 10:13 extended edition of 'All Too Well,' setting a record as the longest track to lead the chart. Don McLean previously held this record starting in 1972, when his 8:36 song 'American Pie' reached the top position.

works.title: American Pie
works.eventDescription: Taylor Swift achieved a No. 1 on the US Hot 100 with the 10:13 extended edition of 'All Too Well,' setting a record as the longest track to lead the chart. Don McLean previously held this record starting in 1972, when his 8:36 song 'American Pie' reached the top position.

Taylor Swift held the No.1 position on the US album chart with her fifth studio album, 1989. Opening-week sales for 1989 in the US marked the highest total for any album since 2002, and the release emerged as the top-selling album of 2014 in the US. Globally, the album has achieved sales exceeding 9 million copies.

works.title: Move It
works.eventDescription: An independent review recommended leaving copyright terms unchanged, resulting in an unsuccessful effort by Sir Cliff Richard to extend the duration musicians receive record royalties. Richard sought a 95-year copyright term instead of the existing 50-year period. In 2008, copyright protection for Sir Cliff's first major hit, "Move It"—recorded in 1958—was set to begin expiring.

works.title: Foot Tapper
works.eventDescription: Tony Meehan, drummer with The Shadows, died at the age of 62 due to head injuries following a fall at his London flat located in Maida Vale. He achieved the 1963 UK No.1 single 'Foot Tapper' along with 28 additional UK Top 40 singles. In 1961, he departed from The Shadows to pursue session drumming work alongside Joe Meek. Additionally, he secured the UK No.1 hit 'Diamonds' in collaboration with Jet Harris.
